title: Rotor fastener grip budget, NAS6403U2H (.125 in)

checks.label: grip budget, NAS6403U2H (.125 in)
excluded_terms: balancing mass thickness (216579-002..-007, 4-66 g each, 0 to a stacked combination up to 80 g per general note 12 / JED02183) -- no part drawing in this repo, only weight is printed

receiving-structure engagement thickness at the tapped hole (216231-002 HUB AND BLADE ASSEMBLY, or whichever of the three reference-balloon assemblies at SECTION T-T actually carries the tapped hole) -- no part drawing in this repo; the balloons here are reference-only (qty '-', no dimension)
checks.guidance: sourced clamped column minus grip. This check carries `complete: false` -- the balancing mass(es) and the receiving structure are both missing from the column, so the verdict is scoped to a BUDGET, not the joint. Read the magnitude instead: it is the combined mass+structure thickness this dash can accommodate before the receiving member would engage the bolt's incomplete threads (JPS00094 5.5.5). At worst case (grip max vs sourced-column min, both zero-width so nominal=min=max=2.413 mm) that budget is 3.429 - 2.413 = 1.016 mm; at nominal it is 3.175 - 2.413 = 0.762 mm. This is the SHORTEST of the nine options and therefore the smallest budget in the family.

provenance.pinned_by: tests/test_topology_conversions.py -- every field of the folded interval must equal that check's, exactly.

notes: The chain walks `fastener_grip_u2h` AGAINST its authored orientation (shank_full_dia_end -> head_bearing_face, sign -1) then the two washer edges WITH their authored orientation (sign +1 each), giving `sourced_clamped_stack - fastener_grip_u2h` -- the same term list the referenced check uses (path term default +1, the fastener element sign -1).

One study per dash, not a shared one: see topology_rotor_fastener_length.json's own notes for why the nine grip options cannot be folded through a single Study's checks list without losing a fastener's own tolerance band.
